description:
The calculator visualises the loan as a principal/interest pie chart and a
  yearly stacked bar chart; both must reflect the underlying numbers.

elements.name: Changing the start month changes the number of bars

steps.name: I open the EMI calculator
I select the "Personal Loan" tab
I enter a loan amount of "10L", an interest rate of 12% and a tenure of 5 years
I change the schedule start month to "2027-01"
the bar chart should have one bar per calendar year of the schedule
I change the schedule start month to "2027-07"
the bar chart should have one bar per calendar year of the schedule

elements.name: Pie chart shows a non-zero principal / interest break-up — 25L @ 10% for 10y

steps.name: I open the EMI calculator
I select the "Home Loan" tab
I enter a loan amount of "25L", an interest rate of 10% and a tenure of 10 years
I submit the loan details
the break-up pie chart should be visible
both pie chart slices should have values greater than zero
the pie chart slices should equal the principal and my calculated total interest
the pie chart legend should show the same values as the slices

elements.name: Bar chart follows the schedule start month and its tooltip shows correct values

steps.name: I open the EMI calculator
I select the "Personal Loan" tab
I set the loan amount slider to "10L", the interest rate slider to 12% and the tenure slider to 5 years
I change the schedule start month to "2026-11"
the yearly bar chart should be visible
the bar chart should have one bar per calendar year of the schedule
every bar should have non-zero principal and interest
the bars' principal should add up to the loan amount
I hover over the bar for 2028
the tooltip should show the 2028 principal, interest and balance from my own schedule

description:
The API should handle boundary and invalid input with appropriate 4xx codes or
  error messages and never fail server-side (5xx).

  JSONPlaceholder is a fake API: it accepts any JSON and echoes it back with
  201. Scenarios tagged @known-defect assert the *expected* behaviour and are
  marked @fail (expected to fail) so the suite stays green while the defects
  stay visible in the report. If the API is ever fixed, those scenarios will
  start "unexpectedly passing" and flag it.

the response should not be a server error

the echoed "title" should be identical to what was sent
the response should arrive within the configured time limit
